meta.purpose: SLATE career depth: awards bodies, wardrobe fittings, performer-furnished wardrobe, deal negotiation, press/promotion obligations.
meta.rules: No invented numbers. Every figure carries a source URL. null means not found in a source that could be read; the note says what is missing. Where a figure came only from a search-engine excerpt of a page that blocked direct fetching (sagaftra.org, backstage.com, bafta.org and deadline.com all returned 403 or paywall redirects), the entry says so in 'verification'.

verificationLevels.primary-read: Read directly from the official rules/agreement document (PDF text extracted locally or page fetched).
verificationLevels.official-excerpt: Official page, but only a search-engine excerpt could be read (page blocked direct fetch).
verificationLevels.trade-excerpt: Trade press or industry secondary source, read via excerpt or fetch.
verificationLevels.unconfirmed: Only a non-authoritative source; treat as provisional.

importantCaveats: SAG-AFTRA ratified a new TV/Theatrical Agreement on 2026-06-04 running 2026-07-01 to 2030-06-30 (3% compounded annual minimum increases). The official 2026 MOA PDF on sagaftra.org could not be fetched (403); 2026 changes below come from SAGindie (a SAG-AFTRA-affiliated site) and GreenSlate summaries, and the base rule text comes from the 2014 Codified Basic Agreement and the 2023 MOA hosted on amptp.org.

SAG-AFTRA's own help-centre answer (servicesagaftra.custhelp.com a_id 997) still states the 2014 cleaning allowances ($18 formal / $12 other per outfit per week). The 2023 MOA raised formal wear to $27; the help page is stale on formal wear.

Several 2026-27 dates (Primetime Emmys 2027, Daytime Emmys 2027, Tony 2027 cutoff/nominations, Olivier 2027 window, IFTA 2027 ceremony, Canadian Screen Awards 2027 nominations/ceremony, Premios Ariel 2027 call) were not yet published by the bodies as of 2026-10-01. They are null with a note; prior-year patterns are given only as labelled patterns, never as dates.

scaleAndScalePlusTen.scale: Union minimum for the job under the applicable agreement.
scaleAndScalePlusTen.scalePlusTen: Offer of scale plus 10% so the agent's 10% commission does not reduce the performer below scale. For SAG-AFTRA theatrical/TV/streaming work an agent must negotiate above scale (generally scale+10) to commission; the +10 is then the agent's entire compensation. For performers well above scale, the agent may commission 10% of gross as long as it does not invade scale.

us.rule: SAG-AFTRA franchised agents (Rule 16(g) regulations): no commission above 10%, cannot be evaded by side fees; no miscellaneous fees.

usManagers.legal: In California a manager is unlicensed and may not procure employment (Talent Agencies Act, Labor Code 1700.4); contracts can be voided and commissions refunded by the Labor Commissioner.

uk.range: 10%-15% typical across TV, film, theatre, commercials; theatre and lower-paid screen 10%-12.5%; commercials/voice-over/overseas often 15%-20%.
uk.vat: VAT (20%) is charged on the commission, not on the fee.
uk.regulation: Employment Agencies Act 1973 and Conduct of Employment Agencies and Employment Businesses Regulations 2003: agents cannot charge a fee for finding work. The Personal Managers' Association publishes a code of practice but no set rate.

agentCommission.canadaNote: ACTRA agent commission norms not found in a readable source.

overscaleAndQuotes.overscale: Any negotiated fee above the union minimum; the minimum agreements set floors only. ACTRA IPA A806 obliges casting directors to negotiate in good faith and not to pressure or coerce performers into accepting only minimum terms, and to negotiate only the engagement at hand.
overscaleAndQuotes.quote: An actor's quote is what they were paid on their most recent comparable job; agents push for an increment each job (reported range USD 2,500 to seven figures depending on medium and profile).
overscaleAndQuotes.salaryHistoryLaw: California Labor Code 432.3 (effective 2018-01-01) bars employers from asking for or verifying salary history; agents may disclose a client's quote only with written consent, and studios may not call to verify.

favoredNations.definition: Most favored nations (MFN / favored nations): no other similarly situated performer on the project may get better terms; if one does, the MFN-protected performer's terms rise to match. Can cover salary, billing, dressing rooms, transport, perks.
favoredNations.whereUsed: Ensemble films and plays, independent films, TV series with several roughly equal leads.
favoredNations.example: Meryl Streep's reported use of favored nations to secure equal pay for Anne Hathaway and Emily Blunt on The Devil Wears Prada 2 (amount reported as USD 2.5 million by a secondary blog; treat as unverified).

guestStarsAndCoStars.topOfShow: Traditionally a guest star was paid 'top of show': the full episode production cycle (8 days for one-hour drama, 5 for half-hour comedy) plus 10%. Under SAG-AFTRA TV rules, a 'Major Role' performer (half-hour or one-hour scripted dramatic series for ABC, CBS, FBC, NBC prime time, The CW, or pay-TV series of that type at Exhibit A rates) gets 10% above the day performer rate for 5 days (half-hour) or 8 days (one-hour). Guest Star, Special Guest Star, Starring or Special Appearance By credit triggers Major Role pay.
guestStarsAndCoStars.trend: Deadline reported guest-star deals increasingly done as 1-3 day stints at discounted pay, sometimes scale for one day, for non-recurring roles.
guestStarsAndCoStars.negotiables: Rate (scale, scale+10, top of show), number of guaranteed days, screen credit wording and placement (which also drives Major Role status), episodic guarantees for recurring roles.
guestStarsAndCoStars.verification: primary-read (wage table); trade-excerpt (practice); 2026-07-01 Major Role figures not read

equityUKCinema2024_25.budgetBand: GBP 3m and over (basic, excluding pre-purchased use fees)

actraIPA_principalActorDaily.note: Rate chart B101(a); 2027 cell extracted as 679.50 which is a PDF layout artifact, not a real figure.

unionMinimumsVsNegotiated.principle: All union figures are floors; above-floor fees, billing, perks and back end are negotiated by agents.

sagAftra.dayPerformersScheduleA: Publicity interviews, whether on a work day or not, are not work time for any purpose; the performer is under no obligation to report for them.
sagAftra.weeklyPerformersScheduleB: Publicity interviews at a mutually satisfactory time are not work time unless held on a day the performer is otherwise working; even then, if after dismissal for the day at a mutually agreed time, not work time. An interview in a meal period is not a meal violation.
sagAftra.publicityStills: Performer agrees to render publicity still services. If the producer wants them unpaid it must get a union waiver; without a waiver, minimum 2 hours' pay then hourly units.
sagAftra.toursAndPersonalAppearances: Transportation per General Provisions §35.D and reasonable expenses paid; producer must ensure adequate rest periods.
sagAftra.promotionalFilms: 30-minute-or-less theatrical promotional films: compensation is individually bargained; performer may agree to appear without compensation (CBA §18.B).
sagAftra.whatCountsAsPromotion: SAG-AFTRA's 2023 strike rules listed covered promotion/publicity services: tours, personal appearances, interviews, conventions, fan expos, festivals, FYC events, panels, premieres/screenings, award shows, junkets, podcasts, social media, studio showcases.
sagAftra.paidUnderUnionMinimums: No separate union minimum for junket days was found. Under the CBA, interviews are not work time; junket participation for principals is governed by the personal services contract, where promotional services are typically included in the guaranteed fee, with travel and expenses paid by the distributor.
sagAftra.section: CBA Schedule A §19-20; Schedule B §23-24; General Provisions §18, §27
sagAftra.verification: primary-read (CBA 2014 text; later MOAs read did not amend these sections); trade (contract practice)

equityUK.rule: Pact/Equity CFA F26.8: during and after the engagement the artist agrees, subject to reasonable professional availability, to perform such reasonable press and publicity services as the producer or its distributors require in any territory, subject only to payment of the artist's reasonable expenses: stills, publicity, interviews (radio, TV, film) and press events. No fee.

irishEquity.rule: Clause 9.6: all publicity and promotion is included in the initial performance fee, subject to availability; during and after the engagement the artist performs reasonable press and publicity services in any territory (stills, interviews incl. radio and TV, press events).

actraCanada.rule: IPA A3201: performer shall be available as reasonably required to promote and publicize the production, ensuring availability for no less than an aggregate of 4 hours. A3203: if the producer wants the performer to make publicity stills, promos or trailers, the performer (not background) is paid at least the scheduled fee with 4 hours included.
actraCanada.rateChartConflictNote: The IPA rate chart PDF lays out A3203 next to 118.50/123.25/127.50 due to column interleaving; the agreement body text gives 680.75/708.00/732.75 and is used here.
actraCanada.promoUseFees: Promotion does not attract use fees on New Media; converting promotional content to a New Media use pays 3.6% of DGR from the first dollar.

junketNorms.format: One concentrated press day or weekend in a single location; press come to talent. Round-robin: broadcast/online video outlets get individual camera slots, rotating crews; print/digital often in roundtables.
junketNorms.tvSlotLength: 4 to 6 minutes per on-camera TV interview (one source); 5-15 minutes generally, some limited to 5-minute slots (others).
junketNorms.interviewsPerDayNote: No documented numeric count found. Sources say only 'dozens of outlets per talent chair' in a full junket day. Not quantified by any union or trade source read.
